key_insight: High-order IMEX BDF–FEM schemes achieve unconditional stability and optimal convergence for a regularized Hodgkin–Huxley model on branched axons without coupling timestep size to mesh spacing.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports accurate, efficient simulation of electrical pulse propagation and splitting in branched neural cables.
method: Combine BDF orders 1–5 with conforming finite elements of any fixed degree p ≥ 1.
Smoothly mask extrapolated gates and cut off voltage-dependent rates to enable stability analysis.
Use one linear voltage solve per timestep, followed by independent nodal gate updates.
evidence_signal: Manufactured solutions recover predicted orders through BDF5–P4, while action-potential simulations and within-family work–precision tests demonstrate propagation, splitting, and lower runtime for higher-order variants along tested refinement paths.
watch_item: The guarantees apply to the regularized model under stated assumptions; numerical quadrature must keep its full residual defect at O(h^{p+1}) to preserve optimal convergence.
paper_title: High-Order Unconditionally Stable IMEX BDF--FEM Schemes for the Hodgkin--Huxley Model on a Branched Axon
